summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships an opaque Go binary implementing a WebRTC remote-control agent
details: The tarball for sextant-cli-linux-arm64@0.0.1-rc33 contains only package.json and a ~12 MB linux/arm64 Go ELF at bin/sxt (sha256 b616fdd0362028d5c6af6897fd123172202067d476537d7ce5e63dbb9d4e02d4); there is no source, no lifecycle hooks, and no bin/main mapping, so the shipped binary is intended to be executed by a parent CLI that lists this as a platform-specific optional dependency. Strings inside bin/sxt include a full pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, datachannel, dtls, sctp, srtp, ice, turn, stun, mdns), coder/websocket, and go-qrcode pairing, together with a hardcoded signaling relay at https://relay.sextant.top plus wss:// and turn: endpoints — the shape of a signaling + data-channel remote-control agent that, once a remote peer is paired, can drive the installer's host over the WebRTC data channel. Additional strings reference http://ip-api.com (public IP geolocation of the host) and https://api.anthropic.com / https://claude.ai, consistent with reconnaissance of the installer and interception/proxying of the installer's Claude session to the remote operator. package.json omits author, homepage, and repository fields and sets license to "SEE LICENSE IN https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control" — a username and repo name inconsistent with the advertised "sxt CLI" purpose and matching the remote-control behavior implemented by the binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
